```{r setup, include=FALSE}

#-----------------------------------------------------------------
# Run first if not already installed

#remotes::install_github("pbs-assess/sdmTMBextra", dependencies = TRUE)

#-----------------------------------------------------------------
# Begin setup
#-----------------------------------------------------------------

rm(list=ls())
gc()

load.lib <- c("tidyverse", "data.table", "cowplot", "sf", 
              "here", "sdmTMB", "sdmTMBextra",
              "future.apply", # required for running sdmTMB::sdmTMB_cv
              "groupdata2", # allows for creation of stratified folds
              "ggforce" # enables plot_anisotropy
              ) 

install.lib <- load.lib[!load.lib %in% installed.packages()]

for(lib in install.lib) install.packages(lib,dependencies=TRUE)
sapply(load.lib,require,character=TRUE)

sf_use_s2(TRUE)

dir <- here(getwd())

source(here(dir, "functions.R"))

```

# Load coastal shapefile and define projection

```{r, ROMS.test}

# Since the data falls within two UTM zones and there is not an ideal projection to use, apply a custom equal area Albers projection
aea_custom <- "+proj=aea +lat_1=30 +lat_2=50 +lat_0=40 +lon_0=-124.5 +datum=WGS84 +units=m +no_defs"

# High res coastal boundary from NOAA
land.barrier <- read_sf(here(dir, "Data", "Shapefiles", "land.barrier.shp"))

# Load YearSeason gaps to fill
load(file = here(dir, "Data", "ExampleRun",
                                    "est.missing.time2.rda"))

```

# Load YearSeason data (with MLD) and calculate density

Note you will need to redefine the transect centres to get X and Y and that you need to adjust the data depending on whether a fixed 30m or mld is used.

```{r, load.seasonal.data.mld}

# Load new sdm data
TwoSeas.dat <- fread(here(dir, "Data", 
                           "mld.final_table_allHistoric.csv"))
# Create transect data
survey.transects.st <- TwoSeas.dat %>%
  select(keys, Year, len.bin, Haul.kg, Season, 
         Fin_sweep.m3, latBin, YearSeas, YearSeas.nm, mean_depth,
         start_latitude, start_longitude, stop_latitude, 
         stop_longitude, Country, Species_weight) %>%
   group_by(keys, Year, Season, Fin_sweep.m3, latBin, YearSeas, 
            YearSeas.nm, mean_depth, start_latitude, start_longitude,
            stop_latitude, stop_longitude, Country, Species_weight) %>%
  summarise(Total_W = first(Species_weight)) %>%
  mutate(FID = keys) %>%
     ungroup() %>%
  select(-Species_weight)

# View(survey.transects.st)

# Note data will be in wgs84
survey.transects3.sf <- 
  make_transect_sf(survey.transects.st, crs = 4326) 

survey.transects3.sf.clip <- survey.transects3.sf %>%
  mutate(X = st_coordinates(st_centroid(.))[,1],
         Y = st_coordinates(st_centroid(.))[,2]) %>%
  filter(Y < 52)

range(survey.transects3.sf.clip$Y)
# [1] 31.3443 51.4088

## Create X Y columns and extract polygon centers
TwoSeas.dat4 <- survey.transects3.sf.clip %>%
  # Project the data to Albers Conical Equal Area
  st_transform(., crs = aea_custom) %>%
  # Extract the centre of the transect (this is in km)
  mutate(X = st_coordinates(st_centroid(.))[,1]/1000,
         Y = st_coordinates(st_centroid(.))[,2]/1000) %>%
  st_drop_geometry() 

range(TwoSeas.dat4$X)
# [1] -341.9713  668.1958

range(TwoSeas.dat4$Y)
# [1] -962.797 1287.434

``` 

# Split data by Season

Note that there is no Canadian data for the spring.

## For Season 2 define spatial boundaries

```{r, sptl.boundaries2}

# Filter the data frame
Season.2.dat <- TwoSeas.dat4 %>%
  filter(Season == "Summer" & !Year %in% c(2009:2011) &
           # To be able to compare with ROMS
           !Year > 2019
         ) 

# Delineate spatial domain
Season.2.dat <- 
  Season.2.dat[Season.2.dat$X >= min(Season.2.dat$X) & 
                 Season.2.dat$X <= max(Season.2.dat$X) & 
                 Season.2.dat$Y >= min(Season.2.dat$Y) & 
                 Season.2.dat$Y <= max(Season.2.dat$Y), ]

# Function to test for values ending in .1
integerFunction <- function(x) {
  abs(x %% 1 - 0.1) < 1e-8
}

vals <- integerFunction(est.missing.time2) 

# Apply the function to filter values ending in .1
est.missing.time.S2 <- est.missing.time2[vals]
est.missing.time.S2
# [1] 2009.1 2010.1 2011.1 2020.1

```

# Group like gear configurations

This is based on the literature and survey reports across the US and Canadian Survey segments. Each group used the same gear configuration and overall strategy, but may have more samples in some years than others. The general gear opening dimensions are also comparable within each group.

```{r, gear.configs}

Season.2.dat <- Season.2.dat %>%
  mutate(GearConfig = case_when(
    Country == "Canada" & Year < 2017 ~ "CADpre2017",
    Country == "Canada" & Year == 2017 ~ "CAD2017",
    Country == "Canada" & Year > 2017 ~ "CADpost2017",
    Country == "USA" & Year < 2011 ~ "USApre2011",
    Country == "USA" & Year >= 2011 & Year < 2015 ~ "USA2011-2014",
    Country == "USA" & Year >= 2015 & Year < 2020 ~ "USApost2014"
  ))

```

# Define offset

```{r, gear.configs}

Season.2.dat <- Season.2.dat %>%
  mutate(LogArea = log(Fin_sweep.m3)
  )

```

# Define study plan

General Steps:

Step 1: The Foundation (Mesh & Barrier)

- Goal: Determine if the spatial "map" needs to respect land boundaries.
- Method: Use Stratified Folds (balancing gear/bins).
- Note: Keep the distribution (e.g., Delta gamma) and covariates constant during this step.

Step 2: The Error Structure (Distribution)

- Goal: Find which family (Delta gamma, Tweedie, etc.) best handles your zeros and variance.
- Method: Use the winner from Step 1 and the same Stratified Folds.
- Note: This is where you check if your choice of "Gear" as a covariate vs. an offset works best with the chosen distribution.

Step 3: The Ecological Signal (Covariates)

- Goal: Determine which environmental variables (temp, depth, etc.) actually improve predictions.
- Method: Use the winner from Step 1 & 2 and the same Stratified Folds.
- Selection: Use ELPD to see if adding a covariate actually adds "information" or just "noise."

Step 4: The Robustness Check (Sensitivity Analysis)

- Goal: Prove your results aren't just a fluke of the fold method.
- Method: Take your Final "Best" Model and run it through Spatial Block Folds or Random Folds.
- What you are looking for: If the model performs well in Stratified but terrible in Spatial Blocks, it means your model is good at "filling in gaps" but bad at "extrapolating." If it performs well in both, you have a very powerful, generalizable model.

# Create folds (this is your most restrictive method)

Note that latBins was chosen based on the general survey sampling designs and the annual catch weight distributions across the 5 areas. The distributions were very similar for for the CalCOFI region so these were grouped together.

Here we combine like-gears and spatial area to ensure that the unique combinations of gear and location are split as evenly as possible across your folds. This is important given the sampling effort is very unbalanced.

Why this "Final Check" is valuable:
In many peer-reviewed journals, reviewers will ask: "How do I know your model isn't just over fitting to the specific locations you sampled?"
By doing Step 4, you can answer: "We selected our model using stratified CV to account for gear differences. To ensure robustness, we also tested it using spatial blocks, which confirmed that our barrier mesh significantly improved the model's ability to generalize to new areas."

```{r, test.folds}

Season.2.dat.w.folds.is.made = T

if (Season.2.dat.w.folds.is.made == F){
  
  set.seed(123) # Lock the shuffle
  # We 'force' the folds to respect the gear/bin combinations
  Season.2.dat.w.folds <- Season.2.dat %>%
    groupdata2::fold(
      k = 5, 
      cat_col = c("GearConfig", "latBin")
      )

  # SAVE THIS DATASET NOW!!!
  ## While it is good practice to set.seed before cross validation,
  ## this is the step where that will cause the starting value to change.
  saveRDS(Season.2.dat.w.folds, "Season.2.dat.w.folds.rds")

}

Season.2.dat.w.folds <- readRDS(here(dir, "Season.2.dat.w.folds.rds"))

dim(Season.2.dat.w.folds)
# [1] 2843   20

unique(Season.2.dat.w.folds$.folds)
# [1] 2 3 1 5 4
# Levels: 1 2 3 4 5

sampFolds <- Season.2.dat.w.folds %>% group_by(.folds) %>% summarise(n = n()) 
sampFolds
# .folds<fctr>  n<int>
#            1	566			
#            2	570			
#            3	566			
#            4	570			
#            5	571	

Zeros <- Season.2.dat.w.folds %>%
  filter(Total_W == 0)

propZeros <- nrow(Zeros)/nrow(Season.2.dat.w.folds)
propZeros
# [1] 0.8617657

```

# Creat Barrier Mesh (without MLD) at 20 km minimum distance

```{r, construct.barrier.mesh.mld.20km.dist}

# Cutoff values control the minimum distance between knots.
## It is generally better to start with a coarser mesh (larger cutoff)
## However there is a tradeoff on spatial predictability (more knots) and
## over fitting the time to process. If the day is irregularly distributed
## you can also try residual-based knot placement
meshTwoSeas.dat3_20 <- make_mesh(Season.2.dat.w.folds,
                              xy_cols = c("X", "Y"), 
                              cutoff = 20) 

# Check number of mesh nodes 
## If greater than >1,000–2,000 nodes, 
## you’re likely in trouble unless you have a lot of RAM.
length(meshTwoSeas.dat3_20$mesh$loc[,1])
# [1] 405

plot(meshTwoSeas.dat3_20)
points(Season.2.dat.w.folds$X[Season.2.dat.w.folds$Total_W != 0],
       Season.2.dat.w.folds$Y[Season.2.dat.w.folds$Total_W != 0], col = 
         "blue", pch = 19, cex = 0.2) 
points(Season.2.dat.w.folds$X[Season.2.dat.w.folds$Total_W == 0],
       Season.2.dat.w.folds$Y[Season.2.dat.w.folds$Total_W == 0], col = 
         "red", pch = 19, cex = 0.2) 

# proj_scaling should match units of (since we are working in m, but density
# is in km, divide by 1000)
barrier2mld_20 <- 
  sdmTMBextra::add_barrier_mesh(meshTwoSeas.dat3_20, 
                                land.barrier, proj_scaling = 1000)

## If greater than >1,000–2,000 nodes, 
## you’re likely in trouble unless you have a lot of RAM.
length(barrier2mld_20$mesh$loc[,1])
# [1] 405

# Example plot code from ?add_barrier_mesh
mesh_df_water_mld_20 <- 
  barrier2mld_20$mesh_sf[barrier2mld_20$normal_triangles, ]
mesh_df_land_mld_20 <- 
  barrier2mld_20$mesh_sf[barrier2mld_20$barrier_triangles, ]

Mesh.with.barrier_mld_20 <-
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = land.barrier) +
  geom_sf(data = mesh_df_water_mld_20, size = 1, colour = "blue") +
  geom_sf(data = mesh_df_land_mld_20, size = 1, colour = "green")

Mesh.with.barrier_mld_20

```

# Compare mesh approaches before modelling

Key Comparison Notes:

- Interpretation: Higher (more positive/less negative) values indicate better out-of-sample predictive performance.
- Scale: Because sum_loglik is a sum across all data points, it is sensitive to your sample size. As long as you use the same folds and same data for every model, these values are directly comparable.

```{r, mesh.output.comparision}

#---------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Run CV with standard mesh with 20 km distance
#---------------------------------------------------------------------

# Fit model
standard_20 <- sdmTMB::sdmTMB(
  Total_W ~ 0 + as.factor(YearSeas),
  data = Season.2.dat.w.folds, 
  family = delta_gamma(type = "standard"), 
  mesh = meshTwoSeas.dat3_20,
  # Fit model by year and month
  ## Note if time is specified, spatiotemporal correlation 
  ## is tested by default
  time = "YearSeas.nm",
  # Use "ar1" or "rw" if you expect temporal autocorrelation
  # Otherwise, use default "iid" (independent by time step)
  spatiotemporal = "iid",
  spatial = "on",
  anisotropy = TRUE,
  #reml = TRUE,
  # Note to keep units the same a grid cell use
  offset = "LogArea",
  #fold_ids = ".folds",
  silent = TRUE
)

# Cross validate
set.seed(27)
# Run the parallel process
plan(multisession, workers = 3) # Keep workers low to avoid RAM crash

cv_standard_20 <- sdmTMB::sdmTMB_cv(
  Total_W ~ 0 + as.factor(YearSeas),
  data = Season.2.dat.w.folds, 
  family = delta_gamma(type = "standard"), 
  mesh = meshTwoSeas.dat3_20,
  # Fit model by year and month
  ## Note if time is specified, spatiotemporal correlation 
  ## is tested by default
  time = "YearSeas.nm",
  # Use "ar1" or "rw" if you expect temporal autocorrelation
  # Otherwise, use default "iid" (independent by time step)
  spatiotemporal = "iid",
  spatial = "on",
  anisotropy = TRUE,
  #reml = TRUE,
  # Note to keep units the same a grid cell use
  offset = "LogArea",
  fold_ids = ".folds",
  silent = TRUE
)
```

# Create summary table

```{r, model.selection.table, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, results = "hide"}

# ====================================================================
# 1. Define Helper Function
# ====================================================================

get_metrics <- function(objs, nm) {
  suite_nm <- if(!is.null(objs$suite)) objs$suite else "Unassigned"
  
  if (is.null(objs$main) || is.null(objs$cv)) {
    return(tibble(
      Suite = suite_nm, Model = nm, `Total ELPD` = NA, 
      `Main Sanity` = "Fit Error", `CV Sanity` = "Fit Error", `Folds Passed` = "0/5"
    ))
  }
  
  res <- try({
    pointwise <- objs$cv$data$cv_loglik
    folds <- objs$cv$fold_loglik
    n_obs <- length(pointwise)
    k_folds <- length(folds)
    
    pw_sd <- sd(pointwise, na.rm = TRUE)
    pw_se <- sqrt(n_obs * var(pointwise, na.rm = TRUE))
    fw_sd <- sd(folds, na.rm = TRUE)
    fw_se <- sqrt(k_folds * var(folds, na.rm = TRUE))
    
    main_s <- all(unlist(sdmTMB::sanity(objs$main)))
    fold_checks <- map_lgl(objs$cv$models, ~ all(unlist(sdmTMB::sanity(.x))))
    
    tibble(
      Suite = suite_nm,
      Model = nm,
      `Total ELPD` = objs$cv$sum_loglik,
      `PW SD` = round(pw_sd, 3), `PW SE` = round(pw_se, 2),
      `FW SD` = round(fw_sd, 2), `FW SE` = round(fw_se, 2),
      `Main Sanity` = if(main_s) "Pass" else "Fail",
      `CV Sanity` = if(all(fold_checks)) "OK" else "! Warning",
      `Folds Passed` = paste0(sum(fold_checks), "/", k_folds)
    )
  }, silent = TRUE)
  
  if (inherits(res, "try-error")) {
    return(tibble(Suite = suite_nm, Model = nm, `Main Sanity` = "Extract Error"))
  }
  return(res)
}

# ====================================================================
# 2. Run the Loop to Collect Data
# ====================================================================

Initial.model.selection.is.made = T

if (!Initial.model.selection.is.made) {
  
  all_results <- list(
    "Standard 20km: Log-link"   = list(main = standard_20, cv = cv_standard_20, suite = "1. Mesh Selection"),
    "Barrier 20km: Log-link"    = list(main = barrier_20,  cv = cv_barrier_20,  suite = "1. Mesh Selection"),
    "Standard 22.5km: Log-link" = list(main = standard_22.5, cv = cv_standard_22.5, suite = "1. Mesh Selection"),
    "Barrier 22.5km: Log-link"  = list(main = barrier_22.5,  cv = cv_barrier_22.5,  suite = "1. Mesh Selection"),
    "Standard 25km: Log-link"   = list(main = standard_25, cv = cv_standard_25, suite = "1. Mesh Selection"),
    "Barrier 25km: Log-link"    = list(main = barrier_25,  cv = cv_barrier_25,  suite = "1. Mesh Selection"),
    "Standard 27.5km: Log-link" = list(main = standard_27.5, cv = cv_standard_27.5, suite = "1. Mesh Selection"),
    "Barrier 27.5km: Log-link"  = list(main = barrier_27.5,  cv = cv_barrier_27.5,  suite = "1. Mesh Selection"),
    "Standard 30km: Log-link"   = list(main = standard_30, cv = cv_standard_30, suite = "1. Mesh Selection"),
    "Barrier 30km: Log-link"    = list(main = barrier_30,  cv = cv_barrier_30,  suite = "1. Mesh Selection"),
    "Standard 32.5km: Log-link" = list(main = standard_32.5, cv = cv_standard_32.5, suite = "1. Mesh Selection"),
    "Barrier 32.5km: Log-link"  = list(main = barrier_32.5,  cv = cv_barrier_32.5,  suite = "1. Mesh Selection"),
    "Standard 35km: Log-link"   = list(main = standard_35, cv = cv_standard_35, suite = "1. Mesh Selection"),
    "Barrier 35km: Log-link"    = list(main = barrier_35,  cv = cv_barrier_35,  suite = "1. Mesh Selection"),
    "Standard 37.5km: Log-link" = list(main = standard_37.5, cv = cv_standard_37.5, suite = "1. Mesh Selection"),
    "Barrier 37.5km: Log-link"  = list(main = barrier_37.5,  cv = cv_barrier_37.5,  suite = "1. Mesh Selection"),
    "Standard 40km: Log-link"   = list(main = standard_40, cv = cv_standard_40, suite = "1. Mesh Selection"),
    "Barrier 40km: Log-link"    = list(main = barrier_40,  cv = cv_barrier_40,  suite = "1. Mesh Selection"),
    "Standard 42.5km: Log-link" = list(main = standard_42.5, cv = cv_standard_42.5, suite = "1. Mesh Selection"),
    "Barrier 42.5km: Log-link"  = list(main = barrier_42.5,  cv = cv_barrier_42.5,  suite = "1.  Mesh Selection"),
    "Standard 45km: Log-link"   = list(main = standard_45, cv = cv_standard_45, suite = "1. Mesh Selection"),
    "Barrier 45km: Log-link"    = list(main = barrier_45,  cv = cv_barrier_45,  suite = "1. Mesh Selection")
  )
  
  # Step A: Combine raw metrics into one dataframe
  summary_df <- imap_dfr(all_results, ~get_metrics(.x, .y))
  
  # ====================================================================
  # 3. Post-Process: Apply Fixed Delta Logic and Hierarchical Ordering
  # ====================================================================
  
  model_decision_table <- summary_df %>%
    # Structural hierarchy layout (Suite -> Model -> Sanity Info -> Total ELPD)
    select(
      Suite, Model, 
      `Main Sanity`, `CV Sanity`, `Folds Passed`, 
      `Total ELPD`, 
      everything() 
    ) %>%
    
    # Calculate relative DELTA ELPD grouped by Suite
    group_by(Suite) %>%
    mutate(
      # Condition: Row must pass both sanity tests and have valid ELPD data
      is_valid_baseline = `Main Sanity` == "Pass" & 
                          `CV Sanity` == "OK" & 
                          !is.na(`Total ELPD`),
      
      # FIX: Target the HIGHEST (most positive/best fit) ELPD among passing models
      baseline_elpd = if(any(is_valid_baseline)) {
        max(`Total ELPD`[is_valid_baseline], na.rm = TRUE)
      } else {
        NA_real_
      },
      
      # Compute Delta (The top model outputs 0, inferior models output negative values)
      `DELTA ELPD` = round(`Total ELPD` - baseline_elpd, 2)
    ) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    
    # Drop calculation columns and position DELTA ELPD next to Total ELPD
    select(-is_valid_baseline, -baseline_elpd) %>%
    relocate(`DELTA ELPD`, .after = `Total ELPD`) %>%
    
    # Sorting: Sort by Suite, then arrange by Delta descending 
    # This places your 0-valued best model at the top of each suite.
    arrange(Suite, desc(`DELTA ELPD`))

  # Print final corrected table
  print(model_decision_table)
}

```

The winner is the standard mesh because the ELPD is larger (the highest value).

## Update summary table with alternative lognormal models

```{r, update.summary.table.with.lognormal, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, results = "hide"}

# ====================================================================
# 2. Run the Loop to Collect Data
# ====================================================================

Alt.Lognormal.Model.is.made = T

if (Alt.Lognormal.Model.is.made == F){
  # Add the new model to the list
  all_results[["Delta lognormal: Poisson-link"]] <- 
    list(main = deltalognormal, 
         cv = cv_deltalognormal, 
         suite = "2. Distribution Family Selection")
  all_results[["Delta lognormal grad.: Poisson-link"]] <- 
    list(main = deltalognormal.grad, 
         cv = cv_deltalognormal.grad, 
         suite = "2. Distribution Family Selection")
  all_results[["Delta lognormal: Log-link"]] <- 
    list(main = deltalognormal.loglink, 
         cv = cv_deltalognormal.loglink, 
         suite = "2. Distribution Family Selection")
  all_results[["Delta lognormal grad.: Log-link"]] <- 
    list(main = deltalognormal.loglink.grad, 
         cv = cv_deltalognormal.loglink.grad, 
         suite = "2. Distribution Family Selection")

# Step A: Combine raw metrics into one dataframe
  summary_df <- imap_dfr(all_results, ~get_metrics(.x, .y))
  
  # ====================================================================
  # 3. Post-Process: Apply Fixed Delta Logic and Hierarchical Ordering
  # ====================================================================
  
  model_decision_table <- summary_df %>%
    # Structural hierarchy layout (Suite -> Model -> Sanity Info -> Total ELPD)
    select(
      Suite, Model, 
      `Main Sanity`, `CV Sanity`, `Folds Passed`, 
      `Total ELPD`, 
      everything() 
    ) %>%
    
    # Calculate relative DELTA ELPD grouped by Suite
    group_by(Suite) %>%
    mutate(
      # Condition: Row must pass both sanity tests and have valid ELPD data
      is_valid_baseline = `Main Sanity` == "Pass" & 
                          `CV Sanity` == "OK" & 
                          !is.na(`Total ELPD`),
      
      # FIX: Target the HIGHEST (most positive/best fit) ELPD among passing models
      baseline_elpd = if(any(is_valid_baseline)) {
        max(`Total ELPD`[is_valid_baseline], na.rm = TRUE)
      } else {
        NA_real_
      },
      
      # Compute Delta (The top model outputs 0, inferior models output negative values)
      `DELTA ELPD` = round(`Total ELPD` - baseline_elpd, 2)
    ) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    
    # Drop calculation columns and position DELTA ELPD next to Total ELPD
    select(-is_valid_baseline, -baseline_elpd) %>%
    relocate(`DELTA ELPD`, .after = `Total ELPD`) %>%
    
    # Sorting: Sort by Suite, then arrange by Delta descending 
    # This places your 0-valued best model at the top of each suite.
    arrange(Suite, desc(`DELTA ELPD`))

  # Print final corrected table
  print(model_decision_table)
}

```

## Update summary table with alternative delta gamma mixed models

```{r, update.summary.table.with.deltagammamixed, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, results = "hide"}

# ====================================================================
# 2. Run the Loop to Collect Data
# ====================================================================

Alt.Deltagammamixed.Model.is.made = T

if (Alt.Deltagammamixed.Model.is.made == F){
  # Add the new model to the list
  all_results[["Delta gamma mixed: Log-link"]] <- 
    list(main = deltagammamix, 
         cv = cv_deltagammamix, 
         suite = "2. Distribution Family Selection")
 all_results[["Delta gamma mixed: p_extreme = 0.01, Log-link"]] <- 
    list(main = NULL, 
         cv = NULL, 
         suite = "2. Distribution Family Selection")
  all_results[["Delta gamma mixed: p_extreme = 0.05, Log-link"]] <- 
    list(main = deltagammamix.05, 
         cv = cv_deltagammamix.05, 
         suite = "2. Distribution Family Selection")
  all_results[["Delta gamma mixed grad.: Log-link"]] <- 
    list(main = NULL, 
         cv = NULL, 
         suite = "2. Distribution Family Selection")
  all_results[["Delta gamma mixed grad.: p_extreme = 0.01, Log-link"]] <- 
    list(main = deltagammamix.01.grad, 
         cv = cv_deltagammamix.01.grad, 
         suite = "2. Distribution Family Selection")
  all_results[["Delta gamma mixed grad.: p_extreme = 0.05, Log-link"]] <- 
    list(main = deltagammamix.05.grad, 
         cv = NULL, 
         suite = "2. Distribution Family Selection")

  # Step A: Combine raw metrics into one dataframe
  summary_df <- imap_dfr(all_results, ~get_metrics(.x, .y))
  
  # ====================================================================
  # 3. Post-Process: Apply Fixed Delta Logic and Hierarchical Ordering
  # ====================================================================
  
  model_decision_table <- summary_df %>%
    # Structural hierarchy layout (Suite -> Model -> Sanity Info -> Total ELPD)
    select(
      Suite, Model, 
      `Main Sanity`, `CV Sanity`, `Folds Passed`, 
      `Total ELPD`, 
      everything() 
    ) %>%
    
    # Calculate relative DELTA ELPD grouped by Suite
    group_by(Suite) %>%
    mutate(
      # Condition: Row must pass both sanity tests and have valid ELPD data
      is_valid_baseline = `Main Sanity` == "Pass" & 
                          `CV Sanity` == "OK" & 
                          !is.na(`Total ELPD`),
      
      # FIX: Target the HIGHEST (most positive/best fit) ELPD among passing models
      baseline_elpd = if(any(is_valid_baseline)) {
        max(`Total ELPD`[is_valid_baseline], na.rm = TRUE)
      } else {
        NA_real_
      },
      
      # Compute Delta (The top model outputs 0, inferior models output negative values)
      `DELTA ELPD` = round(`Total ELPD` - baseline_elpd, 2)
    ) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    
    # Drop calculation columns and position DELTA ELPD next to Total ELPD
    select(-is_valid_baseline, -baseline_elpd) %>%
    relocate(`DELTA ELPD`, .after = `Total ELPD`) %>%
    
    # Sorting: Sort by Suite, then arrange by Delta descending 
    # This places your 0-valued best model at the top of each suite.
    arrange(Suite, desc(`DELTA ELPD`))

  # Print final corrected table
  print(model_decision_table)
}

```

```{r, update.summary.table.with.deltalognormalmixed, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, results = "hide"}

#====================================================================
# 2. Run the Loop to Collect Data
#====================================================================

Alt.Deltalognormalmixed.Model.is.made = T

if (Alt.Deltalognormalmixed.Model.is.made == F){
  # Add the new model to the list
  all_results[["Delta lognormal mixed: Log-link"]] <- 
    list(main = deltalognormalmix, 
         cv = cv_deltalognormalmix, 
         suite = "2. Distribution Family Selection")
 all_results[["Delta lognormal mixed: p_extreme = 0.01, Log-link"]] <- 
    list(main = deltalognormalmix.01, 
         cv = cv_deltalognormalmix.01, 
         suite = "2. Distribution Family Selection")
  all_results[["Delta lognormal mixed: p_extreme = 0.05, Log-link"]] <- 
    list(main = deltalognormalmix.05, 
         cv = cv_deltalognormalmix.05, 
         suite = "2. Distribution Family Selection")
  all_results[["Delta lognormal mixed grad.: Log-link"]] <- 
    list(main = deltalognormalmix.grad, 
         cv = cv_deltalognormalmix.grad, 
         suite = "2. Distribution Family Selection")
  all_results[["Delta lognormal mixed grad.: p_extreme = 0.01, Log-link"]] <- 
    list(main = deltalognormalmix.01.grad, 
         cv = cv_deltalognormalmix.01.grad, 
         suite = "2. Distribution Family Selection")
  all_results[["Delta lognormal mixed grad.: p_extreme = 0.05, Log-link"]] <- 
    list(main = deltalognormalmix.05.grad, 
         cv = cv_deltalognormalmix.05.grad, 
         suite = "2. Distribution Family Selection")

  # Step A: Combine raw metrics into one dataframe
  summary_df <- imap_dfr(all_results, ~get_metrics(.x, .y))
  
  # ====================================================================
  # 3. Post-Process: Apply Fixed Delta Logic and Hierarchical Ordering
  # ====================================================================
  
  model_decision_table <- summary_df %>%
    # Structural hierarchy layout (Suite -> Model -> Sanity Info -> Total ELPD)
    select(
      Suite, Model, 
      `Main Sanity`, `CV Sanity`, `Folds Passed`, 
      `Total ELPD`, 
      everything() 
    ) %>%
    
    # Calculate relative DELTA ELPD grouped by Suite
    group_by(Suite) %>%
    mutate(
      # Condition: Row must pass both sanity tests and have valid ELPD data
      is_valid_baseline = `Main Sanity` == "Pass" & 
                          `CV Sanity` == "OK" & 
                          !is.na(`Total ELPD`),
      
      # FIX: Target the HIGHEST (most positive/best fit) ELPD among passing models
      baseline_elpd = if(any(is_valid_baseline)) {
        max(`Total ELPD`[is_valid_baseline], na.rm = TRUE)
      } else {
        NA_real_
      },
      
      # Compute Delta (The top model outputs 0, inferior models output negative values)
      `DELTA ELPD` = round(`Total ELPD` - baseline_elpd, 2)
    ) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    
    # Drop calculation columns and position DELTA ELPD next to Total ELPD
    select(-is_valid_baseline, -baseline_elpd) %>%
    relocate(`DELTA ELPD`, .after = `Total ELPD`) %>%
    
    # Sorting: Sort by Suite, then arrange by Delta descending 
    # This places your 0-valued best model at the top of each suite.
    arrange(Suite, desc(`DELTA ELPD`))

  # Print final corrected table
  print(model_decision_table)
}
```

# Compare sweep volume vs sweep area*depth offset approaches

## Define offsets

Note that some authors have integrated sweep area over depth sampled, but this is not expected to change the results here. It is kept as a diagnostic (30 m tends to be the recurrent sampling limit of the surveys so this was chosen). MLD is considered here as an offset, but ideally it would be treated as a covariate. Otherwise applied the assumption that the portion of catch is always tied to MLD. Why this works for sampling bias, it forces the model too act within this relationship rather than assess the biological reality.

```{r, offset.definitions}

# Create new offset columns
Season.2.dat.w.folds <- Season.2.dat.w.folds %>%
  mutate(LogArea30 = log(Fin_sweep.m3/30),
         LogAreaMLD = log(Fin_sweep.m3/mean_depth)
  )

```

## Update summary table with lognormal model using alternative offsets

```{r, update.summary.table.w.deltalognormal.alt.offsets, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, results = "hide"}

# ====================================================================
# 2. Run the Loop to Collect Data
# ====================================================================

Alt.Deltalognormal.alt.offset.Model.is.made = T

if (Alt.Deltalognormal.alt.offset.Model.is.made == F){
  # Add the new model to the list
  all_results[["Delta lognormal: Log-link + log(Sweep_Volume/30m) offset"]] <- 
    list(main = LogArea30, 
         cv = cv_LogArea30,  
         suite = "3. Offset Selection")
  all_results[["Delta lognormal: Log-link + log(Sweep_Volume/MLD) offset"]] <- 
    list(main = LogAreaMLD, 
         cv = cv_LogAreaMLD,  
         suite = "3. Offset Selection")
 all_results[["Delta lognormal: Log-link + log(Sweep_Volume) offset (From Suite 2)"]] <- 
    list(main = deltalognormal.loglink, 
         cv = cv_deltalognormal.loglink, 
         suite = "3. Offset Selection")
 
  # Step A: Combine raw metrics into one dataframe
  summary_df <- imap_dfr(all_results, ~get_metrics(.x, .y))
  
  # ====================================================================
  # 3. Post-Process: Apply Fixed Delta Logic and Hierarchical Ordering
  # ====================================================================
  
  model_decision_table <- summary_df %>%
    # Structural hierarchy layout (Suite -> Model -> Sanity Info -> Total ELPD)
    select(
      Suite, Model, 
      `Main Sanity`, `CV Sanity`, `Folds Passed`, 
      `Total ELPD`, 
      everything() 
    ) %>%
    
    # Calculate relative DELTA ELPD grouped by Suite
    group_by(Suite) %>%
    mutate(
      # Condition: Row must pass both sanity tests and have valid ELPD data
      is_valid_baseline = `Main Sanity` == "Pass" & 
                          `CV Sanity` == "OK" & 
                          !is.na(`Total ELPD`),
      
      # FIX: Target the HIGHEST (most positive/best fit) ELPD among passing models
      baseline_elpd = if(any(is_valid_baseline)) {
        max(`Total ELPD`[is_valid_baseline], na.rm = TRUE)
      } else {
        NA_real_
      },
      
      # Compute Delta (The top model outputs 0, inferior models output negative values)
      `DELTA ELPD` = round(`Total ELPD` - baseline_elpd, 2)
    ) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    
    # Drop calculation columns and position DELTA ELPD next to Total ELPD
    select(-is_valid_baseline, -baseline_elpd) %>%
    relocate(`DELTA ELPD`, .after = `Total ELPD`) %>%
    
    # Sorting: Sort by Suite, then arrange by Delta descending 
    # This places your 0-valued best model at the top of each suite.
    arrange(Suite, desc(`DELTA ELPD`))

  # Print final corrected table
  print(model_decision_table)
}

```
# Add covariates

We are still not capturing the upper 75% quantile and need to figure out what is driving that upward trend. Note that fold, mesh, offset, and response variable must be the same across all models when comparing covariates. Essentially, you can only change 1 thing at a time. From the map above, there is not a particular geographic area that is causing the issue so maybe the issue is related to the gear or an environmental covariate we are not capturing.

```{r, update.summary.table.w.deltalognormal.gear.covar, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, results = "hide"}
# ====================================================================
# 2. Run the Loop to Collect Data
# ====================================================================
```

```{r, update.summary.table.w.deltalognormal.mld.covar, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, results = "hide"}
  all_results[["Delta lognormal: Log-link + log(Sweep_Volume) offset + s(MLD, k=5)"]] <- 
    list(main = NULL, 
         cv = NULL,  
         suite = "5. MLD Covariate Selection")
  all_results[["Delta lognormal: Log-link + log(Sweep_Volume) offset + s(MLD, k=3)"]] <- 
     list(main = fit2.1, 
         cv = NULL,  
         suite = "5. MLD Covariate Selection")
 all_results[["Delta lognormal: Log-link + log(Sweep_Volume) offset + s(log(MLD), k=5)"]] <-
    list(main = fit2.2, 
         cv = NULL, 
         suite = "5. MLD Covariate Selection")
 all_results[["Delta lognormal: Log-link + log(Sweep_Volume) offset + s(log(MLD), k=3)"]] <-
    list(main = fit2.3, 
         cv = NULL, 
         suite = "5. MLD Covariate Selection")
 all_results[["Delta lognormal: Log-link + log(Sweep_Volume) offset + poly(MLD, 2)"]] <-
    list(main = fit2.4, 
         cv = cv_fit2.4, 
         suite = "5. MLD Covariate Selection")
 all_results[["Delta lognormal: Log-link + log(Sweep_Volume) offset + MLD)"]] <-
    list(main = fit2.5, 
         cv = cv_fit2.5, 
         suite = "5. MLD Covariate Selection")
 all_results[["Delta lognormal: Log-link + log(Sweep_Volume) offset (From Suite 4)"]] <- 
    list(main = deltalognormal.loglink, 
         cv = cv_deltalognormal.loglink, 
         suite = "5. MLD Covariate Selection")
 
  model_decision_table <- imap_dfr(all_results, ~get_metrics(.x, .y)) %>%
    group_by(Suite) %>%  # This makes Delta ELPD relative to the best in THAT suite
    arrange(desc(`Total ELPD`), .by_group = TRUE) %>%
    mutate(`Delta ELPD` = round(`Total ELPD` - first(`Total ELPD`), 2)) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    select(Suite, Model, `Total ELPD`, `Delta ELPD`, everything())

  print(model_decision_table)

}

```

# Use REML on final model to obtain biomass indices

```{r, run.reml.on.final.model}
# Fit model
deltalognormal.loglink.reml <- sdmTMB::sdmTMB(
```

## Update summary table with reml for biomass indices

```{r, update.summary.table.with.deltalognormal.reml, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, results = "hide"}

# ====================================================================
# 2. Run the Loop to Collect Data
# ====================================================================

Deltalognormal.reml.Model.is.made = T

if (Deltalognormal.reml.Model.is.made == F){
  # Add the new model to the list
  all_results[["Delta lognormal (w/o REML): Log-link (From Suite 5)"]] <- 
    list(main = deltalognormal.loglink, 
         cv = cv_deltalognormal.loglink,  
         suite = "6. Restricted Maximum Likelihood (REML) Selection")
 all_results[["Delta lognormal (w REML): Log-link"]] <- 
    list(main = deltalognormal.loglink.reml, 
         cv = cv_deltalognormal.loglink.reml, 
         suite = "6. Restricted Maximum Likelihood (REML) Selection")
 
  # Step A: Combine raw metrics into one dataframe
  summary_df <- imap_dfr(all_results, ~get_metrics(.x, .y))
  
  # ====================================================================
  # 3. Post-Process: Apply Fixed Delta Logic and Hierarchical Ordering
  # ====================================================================
  
  model_decision_table <- summary_df %>%
    # Structural hierarchy layout (Suite -> Model -> Sanity Info -> Total ELPD)
    select(
      Suite, Model, 
      `Main Sanity`, `CV Sanity`, `Folds Passed`, 
      `Total ELPD`, 
      everything() 
    ) %>%
    
    # Calculate relative DELTA ELPD grouped by Suite
    group_by(Suite) %>%
    mutate(
      # Condition: Row must pass both sanity tests and have valid ELPD data
      is_valid_baseline = `Main Sanity` == "Pass" & 
                          `CV Sanity` == "OK" & 
                          !is.na(`Total ELPD`),
      
      # FIX: Target the HIGHEST (most positive/best fit) ELPD among passing models
      baseline_elpd = if(any(is_valid_baseline)) {
        max(`Total ELPD`[is_valid_baseline], na.rm = TRUE)
      } else {
        NA_real_
      },
      
      # Compute Delta (The top model outputs 0, inferior models output negative values)
      `DELTA ELPD` = round(`Total ELPD` - baseline_elpd, 2)
    ) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    
    # Drop calculation columns and position DELTA ELPD next to Total ELPD
    select(-is_valid_baseline, -baseline_elpd) %>%
    relocate(`DELTA ELPD`, .after = `Total ELPD`) %>%
    
    # Sorting: Sort by Suite, then arrange by Delta descending 
    # This places your 0-valued best model at the top of each suite.
    arrange(Suite, desc(`DELTA ELPD`))

  # Print final corrected table
  print(model_decision_table)
}

```


## Use DHARMa to test goodness of fit on best model

1) Check if the spatial random field has correctly accounted for spatial correlation.
2) Check if delta/hurdle models in sdmTMB are properly handling zero-inflation.
3) Visualize if a more complex model (*e.g.*, adding AR1 spatiotemporal fields) significantly improves the residuals compared to a simpler model. 

```{r, DHARMa.check}

set.seed(27)
# 2. Generate simulation-based residuals (recommended approach)
sim <- simulate(deltalognormal.loglink, nsim = 500, type = "mle-mvn")
r_fit <- dharma_residuals(sim, deltalognormal.loglink, return_DHARMa = TRUE)

# 3. Use DHARMa functions to plot and test
plot(r_fit)

DHARMa::testResiduals(r_fit)
# $uniformity                                                 
# 
# 	Asymptotic one-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov test
# 
# data:  simulationOutput$scaledResiduals
# D = 0.015806, p-value = 0.4763
# alternative hypothesis: two-sided
# 
# 
# $dispersion
# 
# 	DHARMa nonparametric dispersion test via sd of residuals fitted vs. simulated
# 
# data:  simulationOutput
# dispersion = 0.0037314, p-value = 0.004
# alternative hypothesis: two.sided
# 
# 
# $outliers
# 
# 	DHARMa outlier test based on exact binomial test with approximate expectations
# 
# data:  simulationOutput
# outliers at both margin(s) = 6, observations = 2843, p-value = 0.1344
# alternative hypothesis: true probability of success is not equal to 0.003992016
# 95 percent confidence interval:
#  0.0007748782 0.0045878529
# sample estimates:
# frequency of outliers (expected: 0.00399201596806387 ) 
#                                            0.002110447 

Season.2.dat.w.folds$resids <- r_fit$scaledResiduals # from dharma_residuals
ggplot(Season.2.dat.w.folds, aes(X, Y, color = resids)) + 
  geom_point() + 
    scale_colour_gradient2(low = "blue", mid = "grey", high = "red",
                           midpoint = 0.5)

DHARMa::testZeroInflation(r_fit)
# DHARMa zero-inflation test via comparison to expected zeros with simulation
### data:  simulationOutput
### ratioObsSim = 1.0088, p-value = 0.236
### alternative hypothesis: two.sided

# Test spatial autocorrelation 
## 1. Recalculate to group by location
r_aggr <- DHARMa::recalculateResiduals(r_fit, 
                                       group = interaction(Season.2.dat.w.folds$X,
                                                           Season.2.dat.w.folds$Y))
## 2. Get the unique coordinates that match the aggregated residuals
coords_unique <- Season.2.dat.w.folds %>%
  group_by(X, Y) %>%
  summarize(.groups = "drop")
## 3. Run the test
DHARMa::testSpatialAutocorrelation(r_aggr, 
                                   x = coords_unique$X, 
                                   y = coords_unique$Y)
### DHARMa Moran's I test for distance-based autocorrelation
##  data:  r_aggr
##  observed = 0.00020088, expected = -0.00066622, sd = 0.00382222, p-value = 0.8205
##  alternative hypothesis: Distance-based autocorrelation

```

# For summary check

Null Model (M0): Total_W ~ 1 (No random effects, no fixed effects).

```{r, null.deviance}

# 0. Null Model
# Absolute Null: Baseline variance of the data
m0 <- sdmTMB(
  Total_W ~ 1,
  data = Season.2.dat.w.folds, 
  family = delta_lognormal(type = "standard"), 
  mesh = barrier2mld_42.5,
  # Fit model by year and month
  ## Note if time is specified, spatiotemporal correlation 
  ## is tested by default
  time = NULL,    
  # Use "ar1" or "rw" if you expect temporal autocorrelation
  # Otherwise, use default "iid" (independent by time step)
  spatiotemporal = "off",
  spatial = "off",
  spatial_varying = NULL,
  reml = FALSE,
  anisotropy = FALSE,
  # Note to keep units the same a grid cell use
  offset = "LogArea",
  #fold_ids = "fold_idx",
  silent = TRUE
)

sanity(m0)
# ✔ Non-linear minimizer suggests successful convergence
# ✔ Hessian matrix is positive definite
# ✔ No extreme or very small eigenvalues detected
# ✔ No gradients with respect to fixed effects are >= 0.001
# ✔ No fixed-effect standard errors are NA
# ✔ No standard errors look unreasonably large
# ✔ No sigma parameters are < 0.01
# ✔ No sigma parameters are > 100

```

--- THE MATH ---

```{r, deviance.explained.by.component}

d0 <- deviance(m0)
d1 <- deviance(m1_fixed)
d2 <- deviance(m2_sv)
d3 <- deviance(m3_full)

# Percentages of total deviance explained by each:
pct_full_model <- 1 - d3 / d0
pct_fixed_only <- (d0 - d1) / d0
pct_sv_only    <- (d1 - d2) / d0
pct_st_only    <- (d2 - d3) / d0

pct_full_model*100
# [1] 48.72551

pct_fixed_only*100
# [1] 13.23838

pct_sv_only*100
# [1] 16.86159

pct_st_only*100
# [1] 18.62554

```
